claim_corrections.correction: Validation lower-bound tensors are approximately 127.3% OF the torch.mps.recommended_max_memory working set (16183220160 / 12713115648), i.e., approximately 27.3% OVER that working set, not exceeding it by 127.3%.

Do not state that catastrophic swap thrashing or a hard OOM is mathematically guaranteed. The rigorously demonstrated scientific finding is: V15 requires simultaneous tensor payload exceeding both physical RAM and the recommended MPS working set even at the smallest nominal budget (32.84 GB tensor lower bound vs 16 GB RAM / 11.84 GB MPS working set), before excluded overheads; therefore V15 eager production execution is infeasible as written.

The narrative estimate of approximately 10-15 GiB Python parsed-object heap was not directly measured. Retained empirical findings are strictly: PARSED_OBJECT_RESIDENCY_OVERLAPS_TENSOR_RESIDENCY and PEAK_CPU_OBJECT_MEMORY_NOT_EXACTLY_BOUNDED.

The worker-result storage fixture was an approximate structural proxy rather than an exact V14 payload fixture. Storage headroom remains strongly supported (>20x margin over conservative 300 MiB), but exact worker-result byte size will be measured from a canonical non-scientific fixture in V16.
